subject: Re: Integration handoff — SDK bridge, backoff, and endpoint migration
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan@acmeplatform.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena@acmeplatform.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration kickoff + migration constraints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this on. Quick summary from our side: we’re planning a staged cutover from our current vendor to Redwood for generation and embeddings starting late Oct. Key constraints:
- We have strict 200ms P95 latency targets for interactive search paths.
- Many callers are bursty (bot spawns during campaign blasts) — current rate-limit bursts cause 429s.
- We need a non-disruptive endpoint migration path (traffic split, health checks, and quick rollback).

Asks: can you and your CSM/engineer team send a short implementation checklist, recommended SDK timeout/backoff defaults, and a quick sample that shows how to handle 429 + retry-after headers? Also: who owns the cutover window ops?

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Integrations, Acme Platform

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@acmeplatform.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff + migration constraints

Ethan — thanks for the clear summary. Monica will run the success plan and Marcus will own the endpoint migration details; I’ll coordinate the cutover window with your ops lead.

High-level replies to your asks:
- Implementation checklist: attached (redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx) — covers auth, keys, rate-limit tiers, test harness, and rollback steps.
- SDK defaults & samples: see attached markdown + Marcus’ follow-up below — include shorter client-side timeouts for interactive flows and exponential backoff with jitter.
- Cutover ownership: Proposed: Redwood handles router-level split and health-checking, Acme owns traffic ramping on your side. We’ll run a 2hr dry-run prior to production cutover.

Next steps:
1) Monica will share a mutual action plan in the next 24h.
2) Marcus will send exact SDK snippets and the migration play (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
3) Schedule a 60m runbook review with your ops team (please propose two slots).

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

On Tue, Oct 2, 2028 at 09:12 AM Ethan Cole <ethan@acmeplatform.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking this on. Quick summary from our side: we’re planning a staged cutover ...

Hi Ethan — I’m Monica, your CSM. I’ve attached a condensed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) in the checklist and sketched the onboarding milestones below. I’ll track owners and acceptance criteria in HubSpot.

Milestones (high level):
- Week 0: Admin & keys exchange (done via secure DocuSign + KMS verification).
- Week 1: Dev integration — SDK install, API key rotation, smoke tests.
- Week 2: Canary ramp + perf observability verification.
- Week 3: Production cutover + 24h hypercare.

Quick operational guidance for SDK & retries:
- Use a client-side connect timeout = 2000ms, read timeout = 5000ms for interactive routes; background batch jobs can use 10s+.
- Retry policy suggestion (embedded in sdk_timeout_backoff_examples.md):
  * on 429: exponential backoff starting at 300ms, multiplier 2, max backoff 8s; respect Retry-After header when present.
  * on 502/503/504: linear retry with caps and circuit-breaker after 5 failures (10s cooldown).
  * jitter: full jitter is recommended to avoid thundering herd.

Attachments included: examples + a one-page cutover runbook. Marcus will follow with code snippets showing both our Python SDK and a simple curl example for your infra team.

I’ll open the MAP in HubSpot and invite your ops contacts. Proposed runbook review: Wed 2028-10-03 10:00 AM PT or Thu 2028-10-04 02:00 PM PT — which works?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Oct 2, 2028 at 02:18 PM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick operational guidance for SDK & retries: ...

Ethan / team — Marcus from Redwood infra here. Below are the concrete snippets and migration notes I recommend for your engineers.

1) Minimal curl + handling 429:

curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"search refinement\", \"max_tokens\":64}'

Server 429 handling (pseudo):
- If response has Retry-After: parse seconds and sleep that duration.
- Else: backoff = min(8000, base * 2**attempt) with full jitter.

2) Python SDK example (simplified):

import time
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RetryPolicy

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"<API_KEY>\")
retry = RetryPolicy(on_429=True, base_ms=300, max_ms=8000, multiplier=2, jitter='full')
client.set_retry_policy(retry)

try:
    resp = client.generate(prompt='search refinement', timeout=5.0)
except Exception as e:
    # bubble up or circuit-breaker hook
    raise

3) Migration play (canary):
- Step 0: Deploy Redwood endpoint behind router with health-check endpoint /_health returning 200 within 150ms.
- Step 1: 5% traffic for 30m — validate P95 latency and error budget (<=1%).
- Step 2: 25% for 1h — run synthetic traffic and real user sampling.
- Step 3: 50% for 1h — monitor token cost and prefix caching hit rates.
- Step 4: Full cutover and 24h hypercare.

Notes & tips:
- Use per-route client timeouts: interactive routes shorter, batch routes longer.
- Enable prefix caching on requests that reuse prompts to reduce token spend and latency.
- For streamed responses, prefer short read timeouts and ensure your client supports partial frames — we recommend buffering up to 2s before failing.
- If you see >0.5% of requests with Retry-After > 3s during canary: pause traffic and increase batch size or fall back to a cheaper model variant.

Attachments: sdk_timeout_backoff_examples.md (includes code & math), rate_limit_config.diff (router-side rate-limit policy templates).

Proposed cutover window: Mon, 2028-10-09 02:00–06:00 PT (low traffic). Please confirm by EOD and share the ops participant list.

— Marcus Lin
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
